posts.name: j1hopki1
posts.cooked:
I'm sorry, but Mr. Fixer is the worst hero, however you want to define worst. A lot of people point to his low damage output and lack of ongoing and equipment destruction. Others counter those points with cases when he is good. But, the fundamental problem that everyone is missing is once he has a stance and a tool in play he has 16 cards (19 if you count Meditation) in his deck that he can't play without getting rid of one of them. That sucks no matter what situation he is in because using your play phase to put a tool into play and then losing a tool from play is hugely inefficient. The only other hero that comes close to this inefficiency is once AZ has both modules he has 6 cards in his deck he can't play. I've argued against AZ before and don't want to restart that because Fixer is so much worse.

 

Mr. Fixer has to have a way to use his extra cards. I've played where we allowed him to have up to two stances in play. That was a lot of fun.

 

I also love The_Jakey's suggestion on http://sentinelsofthemultiverse.com/forum/topic/does-mister-fixer-need-fixing. It lets him choose the right tool or stance at one time, but change it up later without wasting a play phase.

He suggests: "All styles, like tools, return to your hand if you put another style into play. Strike: You may play a tool or style. Deal one target 1 melee damage."

 

My suggestion is: "Strike: You may discard any number of cards. Mr. Fixer deals one target X melee damage where X=the number of cards discarded plus 1."

posts.name: j1hopki1
posts.cooked: In my previous post I didn't make it clear that only one of the three suggestions should be used. Either two stances OR The_Jakey's idea OR discard to boost. All three together would make him way too good. I want a balanced game because the close battles are always the most fun. I dislike over powered heroes just as much as under powered ones. If this was a post about Tempest and Wraith being too good I'd be just as vehement.

posts.name: TheSoundOfTrees
posts.cooked:
I will try to say things less vehemently than you, and then will mortify myself by becoming a simple lurker.

Mr Fixer is not an easy hero to understand. He asks for a very specific way of thinking, for tactics very different from what we use with most other heroes.

His two card structure, and the number of replacement in his hand, make him very resilient to ongoing/equipment destruction. If he loses something vital, Meditation and Salvage Yard allow him to get it back easily. He does not need a big hand, and so easily sacrifices it for the sake of the team when discards are needed.

The trick with him is not to keep the same styles and tools for all the game - he changes them as needed. He is a Zen guy, and is not emotionaly attached to his cards .

This is not anecdotal evidence : it is the way I, and some others, play him, and by playing this way, what at first seems to be unbearable weaknesses are outshined by his strengths.

He is not the only hero that can seem weak, or counterintuitive, at first, until you understand how he is "supposed" to work. Absolute Zero is seen by some as a weakling, by others as one of the more potent heroes in the game. Many players have conceded that they thought Nightmist bad at first, because of her self inflicted damage and her habit to discard cards. Tachyon and Unity both discard many of their cards without using them, to power their own tactics. All the heroes ask for you to take the right "state of mind" to play them effectively. Mr Fixer's role and tactics are one of the harder to grasp (Expatriette too, it seems).

For me, discovering the "good" way to use what he has was a puzzle I enjoyed solving (and I don't think I've entirely grasped it yet). And I will repeat it vehemently : he is now a hero I enjoy having in a team, not a dead weight.

Of course, we can change his power, to make him easier to play. But I find more interesting to compare our ideas and tactics about how to best use what he already has. Both Fixer and Expatriette are challenging heroes, yes, but very gratifying once you understand them.

But you are firmly convinced Mr Fixer is simply a bad hero, and I know I won't change your mind. So I'd better activate Stealth.
